utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind the witness of the affirmation he made which still applies to his evidence. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. M-056. You surely remember that last Friday we ended that part of your testimony by discussing the unit of the Ministry of Interior, which is called posebna, special unit, and then I showed you some documents, which speak about that unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to that the witness is shown again the Exhibit P75, page 3, 042462, and the English page is 0424692-ET. And that document -- but before that, I apologise, Your Honours, we would need to give the witness again the documents in the court binder so the witness can follow my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document is in tab 14. And as you replied to my question last Friday, all changes in this unit as well as in the other units are therefore governed by a certain general act, a decision, a ruling, or a rule book; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the last page of this document, which is R0424695 in Macedonian, and in English it is R042-4694-ET. And here, in the first paragraph, in middle of it you can see that it speaks about a change in the amount of the salary that the members of this unit receive. So if you see this word here, "posebna," special unit has the right to an increased salary for 20 per cent, that is in the middle of the first paragraph. Then practically this change is only harmonisation of the salary for the members of the posebna special unit with the salaries received at that time with the special unit Tigers. Is that the change that you see written in this decision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if there would be anyone who would claim before this Court that this document refers to the unit Lions, then such assertion would be incorrect. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask now that this document under the number 1D205, which is a decision about the establishment of the posebna unit is received into evidence as Defence exhibit. I apologise. It seems that was the last thing that we did on the Friday. The document has already been given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You recall, Mr. M-056, that on the Friday we discussed and you testified when asked by the Prosecutor that the police units in the joint operations were under the command of the army. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in the tab 2. Its number is 1D222, Macedonian 1D2373, while the English version is 1D2374. This is one more document or one more decision issued by president of the Republic of Macedonia, dated the 4th of July, 2001.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 4th of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The item 1 of the decision stipulates in the last paragraph, the third paragraph, that the deputy chief of the national headquarters of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, lieutenant-general, Pande Petrovski is assigned as the commander of the operation and the commander of the 1st Corps was Major-General Gjorgi Karakutovski is assigned as his deputy. Could you agree with me that this decision again reaffirms your testimony that in the operations that were organised jointly by the army and the police, the command over the operations and over the units belonged to the military commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would seek to tender this document as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D58, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you on Friday few video-clips. One of them was a drill, an exercise of the police and the army units. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the video-clip, you were able to see that that was the time-period around the late Autumn because all the participants were wearing warm clothes, if you remember the video recording, and obviously their surroundings did not appear to be summertime, it, rather, resembled late Autumn. If I were to tell you that this exercise was an exercise at Penus in November 2001, would you be able to agree with me that it was exactly that exercise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is that exercise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also shown a video-clip while you recognised Goran Mitevski and you stated that during that time he was a director of the public security bureau, and you surely recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Is it correct that the director of the public security bureau is appointed by the government of the Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the director is appointed by the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if someone would testify before this Tribunal that the director of public security bureau is appointed by the minister, that testimony would be incorrect. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it would be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We would move now to a completely different area that you discussed with my learned colleague the Prosecutor and that is the issue of the Lions, do you remember that you talked about the rapid deployment battalion, named the Lions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown the document dated 6th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I asked that the witness is shown again that document, P275, and that document is located in your binder in tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You remember that this document was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this document, please focus your attention, this document is actually an order to appoint the units of the Ministry of Internal Affairs that will become part of the temporary joint unit for combat against terrorism. That is the order that you have in front of you. In the first paragraph of this order, the composition of the temporary joint unit for combat against terrorism is established, and this order establishes that this unit will composed of the police rapid deployment or rapid intervention battalion as well as the unit for special tasks of the ministry of internal affairs. Do you see that in this paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This unit for special tasks is actually the Tigers unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the preamble to this order, and in line 2 at the end, you see that this order was brought on the basis of a decision of the government of the Republic of Macedonia to establish a unit for special purposes, confidential number 98/1 of the 12th of June, 2001, and part 1, item 1, 2 of the decision by the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you see that this is what is written in the preamble and this is the grounds on which the Minister Boskoski issued the order that you see in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document that is behind tab 16, and that is P74, actually. Macedonian number R0424682, while the English number starts with 042-4682-ET, first page, 01. Would you please look at the upper left corner. This title here, I should call it, where one can see that the Ministry of the Interior under the number 16.1-4475/1 also dated on the 6th of August, 2001, brought the decision that -- which is written in the middle of the page in capital letters, and this is a decision to establish a rapid intervention police battalion of the ministry of internal affairs. Do you see this, that it is the 6th of August when the aforementioned decision was issued?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the preamble to this decision, you can also see at the end of line 2 that this decision as well was issued on the basis of the decision of the government of the Republic of Macedonia to establish a unit for special purposes, confidential number 98/1, of 12th of July, 2001, and on the basis of the decision of the president of the Republic of Macedonia to establish a temporary unit for combat against terrorism of classification

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that the grounds upon which the minister of the interior issued the aforementioned decision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the grounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you answered to the questions of the Prosecutor on Friday, you stated that the Tigers had 120 members and you also explained that the Tigers were not fully prepared for all conditions of combat against terrorists, especially not for combat in mountainous areas. Do you remember that you testified about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, would it be correct if I were to stay that it was precisely the conditions of the combat against terrorist groups were the reasons why the government and the president of the state issued a decision to establish an additional unit in order to be able to establish the public law and order in the country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, we will come back to this decision again, but I would -- I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 18. That is 1D215, Macedonian 1D2359 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 2329, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While English 1D2331. This is a document of the government of the Republic of Macedonia dated 13th of June, 2001, confidential number 98/1. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is the letter, the cover letter of the Secretary-General of the government of the Republic of Macedonia which accompanies the letter to the Ministry of Defence and, at the same time, you can see the attachment at the bottom on the left-hand side that this decision was also forwarded to the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to turn the page, 1D3 -- 2330, and English 1D2332. And as you can see, this is the text of the decision to establish a special purposes unit. I would like to ask you now to look at paragraph 6 of this decision where the government practically suggests the establishment of this unit together with the army. In paragraph 6 it says: "The order for the use of the special purposes unit will be issued upon the recommendation or proposal of the coordinating body for crisis management by the president of the republic." You do agree with me that considering that the establishment is proposed or the establishment of a unit together with the army is governed here, that before such decision is made, a decision must be made by a supreme commander of the army and that would be the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you to look at the document in tab 19. And that is 1D216, Macedonian, 1D2333, while the English version is 1D2336.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before, Your Honours, I continue asking questions to the witness, I wish to just clarify. This document is something that we found in the 65 ter list of the Prosecutor, but in the 65 ter list there is only the first page of the document, which would be absolutely inappropriate to use in the course of the cross-examination of the witness, so we requested, therefore, a translation of the entire document, and we also submitted for translation the decision that we received from the competent bodies of Macedonia and therefore we will seek to tender this as Defence exhibit after I ask several questions of this witness about this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This decision consists of three pages. The Macedonian version begin in 1D2333 and ends with 1D2335, while the English version begins with 1D2336 an ends with 2337. Again, I would like to ask you when you look at this first page to confirm that this is document issued by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, which is D number 07-54 of the 15th of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The number stands for confidential number, interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And let me just mention, Your Honours, considering that this is a document that is of highly confidential nature that it is not shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you confirm, Mr. M-056, that this document, if you look at the last page of it, which is the Macedonian 1D2335, a decision issued by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the second page of this document, 1D2334, and the English is 1D2337, and I will ask you to look around the middle of this page, the paragraph 1.2 where it says: "From the Ministry of the Interior." Already on the first page you saw that this was a decision issued by the president to establish a temporary units to combat terrorism of Class A. And you saw that on the previous page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the section that I did not show you, the president establishes which are the army units which should become part of this unit, while here, in item 1.2, it is established which are the units that the Ministry of Interior needs to establish in order to make them a part of the temporary joint unit. In line 2, it says that a special tasks unit is established and that it is incorporated into the special operations detachment. It also stated here that the composition of this unit for special purposes should be determined by the Ministry of the Interior. Is that what is written here in the decision of the president?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is written.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, secondly, as the decision orders, a police battalion should be established from within the ranks of the Ministry of the Interior, which will also become part of the unit to combat terrorism, while the composition of the -- of that battalion will be determined by the Ministry of the Interior. Is that what is written in this decision and what is actually an obligation for the Ministry of the Interior as an implementation of the decision of the president of the state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you again to go back to the decision which can be found in tab 16, and that is P74. And it has the Macedonian version number R0424682 and the English page starts with 042-4682-ET, page number 1. Yesterday we were discussing how these units are being established and I would like to ask you, is it correct that the unit that is to be established by the president's decision, it is necessary for a decision to be adopted for its establishment in order to define the composition of this unit, the conditions for the fulfilment of the unit, et cetera. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at item number 3 on the decision for the establishment of the police battalion issued by the president of the state under paragraph 3, you can see that the minister is the one who decides on the composition of this battalion, and it reads that the police battalion for rapid intervention composes of members of the special unit, the unit posebna, from the Ministry of the Interior. Then members of the reserve and members from the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Honourable Judges, since the interpretation that was omitted a bit earlier, item number 3 on the second -- the beginning of the second line, the posebna unit was interpreted as special unit, I think that after the clarification that we're going to get from this testimony regarding the units from the MOI, that these errors in the documents are going to be corrected later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So as we read now under paragraph 3, Mr. M-056, with this decision, the Ministry of Interior, in accordance with the decision by the president of the state, determined the composition of the rapid intervention battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you look at the second page of this very same decision. It is R044683, and in the English version 042-4682-ET-02. And if you pay attention on item number 4, can you see that the minister prescribes the manner in which these police battalion is to be fulfilled for rapid intervention, and this is done in the following manner: On a voluntary basis and by so action from the unit posebna from the Ministry of the Interior. Also, in paragraph 2, it reads that: "This composition will originate the composition that comes from the reserve within the Ministry of Interior will be employed with the minister of interior." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that part of the policemen who are members of the unit posebna are already employed with this decision also it is being determined that one portion of the reserve that will become part of the rapid intervention battalion will be hired, that is to say, employed at the ministry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if somebody would say before this court that the members of this battalion have been employed or reached the employment directly with the minister would not be correct because the decision clearly says that they are going to be employed by the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After this decision that -- within which the minister defined the general condition regarding the composition and the procedure of the establishment, he already mentioned that it was necessary to adopt by-laws for the systemization of the job position, the conditions and the procedure for hiring people, and that is why I would like to ask you to answer several questions pertaining to this procedure of establishment of the aforementioned unit. I would like to ask you now to look the document which can be found in tab 26. This is 1D2321, the English version -- no, no, I'm sorry. I was -- so 1D219, document in tab 26, the Macedonian version, 1D2353, and the English version 1D2355. And if you would agree with me, the Ministry of Interior was adopted the rules on amendments and additions to the rules on the organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior in September 2001. This is what can be read on this first page. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we please turn to the second page. This is the second page of the document also in English, 1D2354. 2356 is in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The rules on the organisation and the operation of the Ministry of Interior, on the 5th of September, 2001, is changed in the following manner. Within these rules the rapid intervention battalion is included, and for the first time it receives the title Lions. Can you see that, item number 5.1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when the Lions have been established, the rapid intervention battalion, the whole procedure for the establishment had to be completed in order for this unit to start to operate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at the document under tab number 20, 1D220, 1D2357 is the Macedonian page, and 1D2364 is the English page. These are the rules on amendments and additions to the rules on the systemization of workplaces of the Ministry of the Interior which had to be in accordance with the changes to the rules on the organisation and the operation of the ministry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the folder, the third page, and this is 1D2359 in the Macedonian version, and in the English version this would be page 1D2366. At the very top you can see item 5.1, rapid intervention battalion-Lions. Therefore, in order for the Lions unit to be established following the changes to the rules on their organisation and the operation, the rules on the systemization of the work positions had to be changed, also to establish the special rapid intervention battalion as such, and determine all the job positions; that is to say, all the positions that have to exist in this particular unit, and the conditions for the hiring of these kind of people. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these rules actually define these conditions. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you now to look at the document in tab 21. This is the Prosecutor's P82, Exhibit P82. The first page, The Macedonian R 042-4685 and the first English page R 042-4685-ET. These rules, I believe you would agree with me, it was adopted in Skopje in October 2001 and it represents the conditions and the procedure for the assignment, rights and duties of the members of the rapid intervention battalion of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the second page of this document, also the second page of this document in the English version. Under item number 2 you see the title, conditions and procedure for assignment in the battalion, and Articles 2, 3, and on the third page, Article 4, determine or stipulate the procedure and the conditions for the appointment and assignment in the battalion, the members, basically in the same manner as we could see that this is determined for the special unit Tigers as well. Is that correct? ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when all these documents have been adopted, then it was possible to open the employment tender, to send people for training and to establish the rapid intervention battalion. Do you agree with me that prior to October 2001, the rapid intervention battalion, Lions, did not exist nor it was possible for it to exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I fully agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The decision by the minister of 6th of August, 2001 was just the beginning of the establishment of this unit by which the conditions have been laid down that are to be followed for the establishment of this unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if somebody, Mr. M-056, would claim that the Lions used to exist during August, this would be simply untrue and impossible; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if someone would claim that the Lions have been present in Ljuboten on 12th of August, 2001, would this would be a completely untrue, and it would be impossible because they were not established and did not exist prior to October 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now I would like to ask you, as our evidence, to tender the exhibits 1D215, this is the decision by the government; 1D216, the decision by the president, one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... time, Ms. Residovic, not all together. And if you could indicate the tab number at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. First of all, I would kindly ask you to accept 1D215, the decision by the government, which can be found in tab 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D59, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I would tender as an exhibit 1D216, the decision by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, in tab 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D60, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I would propose as an exhibit of the Defence to accept 1D219. This is the rules for the changes and amendments of the rules on the organisation of the work of the Ministry of Interior, which can be found in tab 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D61, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I would seek to tender in exhibit 1D220, this is the rules on changes and amendments to the rules on systemization of work positions of the Ministry of Interior, which is in tab 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D62, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-056, is it correct that back in 2003, following the completion or the end of this crisis, a decision has been made to reorganise the rapid intervention battalion, Lions, and an order has been made because there was a need for the joint unit of the army and the police to cease to exist. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the document under tab 22. 1D221, 1D2371. This is in the English version, 2372. And the date, 3rd of January, 2003. You can see that this is an order for terminating of the validity of the order on determining units of the Ministry of Interior which are part of the composition of the temporary joint unit to combat against terrorism. And under paragraph 1 at the very end, this order refers to the document DT 16.1-4476/1, dated 6th of August, 2001, and if you recall, this was the exhibit by the Prosecution shown to you yesterday. Can you see that in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that by this order the order was terminated by which the joint unit was supposed to be established together with the army of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you know this, bearing in mind the position that you held at that time at the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is known to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-056, that at the same time, there were certain changes in the battalion for rapid intervention and that this battalion continued to exist, however, under a different title and a changed composition. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what is the title of this particular unit right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fast response unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would propose now for this document 1D221, which is in tab 22 also to be accepted as an exhibit by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As Exhibit 1D63, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now before you move on, can I ask you about tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document, P275, this is why I did not propose for this document to enter in evidence again and this decision basically eliminate this decision from the 6th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So it is already Exhibit P275, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was accepted into evidence on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-056, as you can see, I have spent a lot of time asking questions related to the composition and the conditions for the establishment of these units, and your answer that you know certain competences of the ministry, now I would like to ask you to answer several questions related to certain competences of the Ministry of Interior. Mr. M-056, please tell me, is it correct that the Ministry of Interior is composed of two rather clear structures, or two parts, the part in charge of public security, and the second part in charge of state security issues. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the composition of the MOI.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that each of these parts of the Ministry of the Interior is headed by a director? So a director of the bureau of public security and a director for state security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you stated a while ago, that the director for public security is appointed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia. It is also the government of the Republic of Macedonia who appoints the director for state security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the parliament of Macedonia also has a special committee that performs the control over the work of the state security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the competences, the duties and responsibilities of the individual bodies, divisions, administrations, departments, or sections are governed by the rule book on organisation and operation of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will show the witness now the document which is essentially the rule book on organisation, operation of the Ministry of Interior, but before that, I wish to say that the Prosecutor has tendered and it was received as P-- as Exhibit P33, the rule book on organisation, operation of the Ministry of Interior. However, the Prosecutor had his own reasons for tendering only one part after that rule book of four pages, while this rule book contains eight pages. The Defence has submitted the entire rule book for translation, and considering that translation hasn't been completed yet, we have a working translation now of two articles only that I wish to discuss now with this witness and when the entire rule book is translated we will seek to tender the entire rule book as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 23. That is 1D217, 1D2338, Macedonian version, and 1D2398, English version. You do agree with me, Mr. M-056, that actually this rule book establishes the organisation or structure, the operation and the competences of individual bodies and units but also its link towards the directors for public security and for state security as well as towards the minister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This rule book on organisation and operation of the Ministry of the Interior was adopted in January 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to ask know that the witness is shown P33, Prosecution Exhibit. We do not have this document within our court binder. And I would like to ask to have the last page of this document displayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see now that this document was adopted on the 21st of June --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, interpreter's correction, 26th of January, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that it was assigned by the then Minister of the Interior Dokta Dimovska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can also see in Article 28 that a component of this document is also the organisational chart of the Ministry of the Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We could now move away from this document. It is important for what I wanted to show you in the document that you have in front of you in tab 23, so I would like to ask now to go back to 1D217 and to display now the page 1D2339, while the English page is 1D2399. Mr. M-056, I would like to ask you to look together the Article 21 of this rule book where it is stated that certain organisational forms of the ministry, that individual organisational forms of the ministry and bureau for public security as a body within the ministry, that --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, I will read exactly as it is written. I will not interpret it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it reads here: "The individual organisational forms of the ministry and the public safety bureau as a body within the ministry are managed by heads whose title and working place are determined by the book of rules on systemization of the working places within the Ministry of Interior Affairs and depending on the type of the organisational scope." It reads in paragraph 2: "The heads of the department for police and the department for crime police and the heads of the analytics and investigations sector, the anti-terrorism sector, the helicopter unit, the records department, the sector for fire protection, the sector for defence preparations are functionally connected with the head of the public safety bureau and are responsible immediately before the head for the operation and the tasks in their area." Is this the paragraph that establishes the actual line of command responsibility and control within the public security bureau?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The paragraph 3 says: "The commander of the special tasks unit, Tiger, and the heads of the internal control department, the department for international cooperation and European integration, the operative techniques sector, the finance sector as well as other joint works, the sector for legal and staff matters, the telecommunications sector, encryption protection and IT and the sector for administrative advisor works with functionally connected with the minister and are responsible for its work and for the tasks in their area." This rule book then establishes the parts of the ministry which are connected to the minister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The paragraph 3 of this document states that the commander of the special tasks unit, Tiger, and the heads of the department for internal control, the department for international cooperation and European integration, the operative techniques sector, the finance and other joint works sector, then the sector for legal and staff matters, the telecommunication sector, the encryption protection and IT and the sector for administrative supervisory works are operation connected also with the head of the public safety bureau and the head of the safety and counter-intelligence department. So when it comes to the Tigers unit, it was linked also to the director for public security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 22 of this rule book that is part of your binder stipulates that the heads of the organisational forms --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I'm not really sure ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Heads of the organisational forms within the other organisational forms are directly responsible before the heads of those organisational forms. The employees, executors are responsibility before their immediate head and the head of the organisational form to which they belong, for the correct execution of their works and tasks. Is this the way in which the competence and the responsibility in the Ministry of Interior was established in accordance to the rule book of January 2001.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as we saw a few moments ago from the -- from the Prosecutor's Exhibit P33, a component was also a chart, so I would like to you look at 1D2342 of the Macedonian version, and the English version is 1D2401. So this one is 1D217 and the number of pages are 1D -- 1D4-- I apologise, 1D2342, the Macedonian version, and 1D2401, the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, while tendering into exhibit this document, we have -- we have objected the chart proposed by the Prosecution and the Prosecution has withdrawn that chart and now the chart you have before you is a component of the rule book which we will tender into exhibit after it has been translated fully and it will replace our exhibit which was tendered today and this demonstrates the way in which -- demonstrates the links within the interior ministry itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. M-056, I would like to ask you to look at this chart and to see only few things, to go through a few things in this central part in this top table. It reads the bureau of the public safety bureau and there are all these organs and sectors which are responsible for the public safety as it has -- as it is prescribed by the rule book. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And here we can see that one part is composed by the crime police which is headed by the head for crime police and on the right hand, we have the department for police. Is this correct? Which is also headed by a head of the department for police which later on becomes an under-secretary for police. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this sector or department for police on the bottom it reads sector for posebna units. Would you agree with me that in January 2001 the only posebna unit was -- on which you have testified today. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And from what we read in Article 21 from the rule book, on the right-hand side, we can see that on the very top we can see the special tasks unit, Tiger, which with this bold line is connected to the Ministry of Interior Affairs, and, at the same time, it is connected with public safety director, and this is what is contained in the Article 21 of the rule book. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-056, that all these changes to the rule book were also accompanied by a modified charts which have shown in which way the organisation within the ministry have been modified and the relations among the different sectors have changed. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe it is time now? No, I apologise. It is not time. I'm sorry. I was thinking of the way as we are working in the morning usually. Now I would like to tender this document in exhibit as a Defence exhibit. And when the -- when the Defence will receive the whole translation we'll put on this number the whole document with a whole translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, I didn't get the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it practical for it to be tendered now or should we await the full translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, we can only note it now and since we will be speaking about this document with other Prosecutor's witnesses, until then we might receive the translation. Then we could tender it as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you like it to be marked for identification now?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be now marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As Exhibit 1D64, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you, Mr. M-056, to look at the document in tab 24. This is document 1D218, the Macedonian version is 1D2347, and the English version is 1D2403. This is a rule book on corrections and additions to the book of rules of organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior Affairs, which was adopted in Skopje in June 2001. If you look at page 1D of 2408 and one -- of Macedonian version and 1D of 2404, this book of rules in June 15 2001, was signed by the minister of interior affairs, at that time, Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as can you see in Article 2 of this rule book, a new sector was established for operative reconnaissance, with a few subdepartments which will be existing in the framework of the sector. Is it what this Article 2 is saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to look at the following page, 1D2409, and the English page is 1D2405. These changes are -- of the rule book, it's accompanied by a chart containing all the changes that have occurred in the organisation and work of the ministry. Can you see that this sector now is included in the chart before you? This is on the right-hand bottom, which is connected to the minister, so on the bottom this chart, a sector for operative reconnaissance was added. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the top of this chart, which is connected to the minister we still have the Tiger special tasks unit. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, in June, in the department for police which can you see within the public safety bureau on the bottom where it writes sector for posebna units, there are no changes, nor any new unit was established. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like this document, 1D218, books of rules for corrections and additions to the book of rules of organisation of the work of Minister of Interior affairs, to tender as exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document at tab 24 will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D65, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. M-056, I would like to ask to you look at the document in tab 25. This is document 1D213, the Macedonian version, 1D2321, and the English version is 1D2407. Before I ask you questions related to this rule book, could you -- do you recall that on Friday we spoke about the transmission of the competences from the minister to the head of police concerning the special unit Tigers, the under-secretary of police. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was in accordance with a request from -- of a commander of special tasks unit, Goran Zdravkovski in July 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at this book of rules on changes of the organisation of the work of the Ministry of Interior affairs from August 2001 and to look at the page 1D2322, and the English version 1D2408. In Article 1 of book of rules on changes of the book of rules of organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior affairs, can you see in line 3 from the bottom, that -- that item 1 is changed from Article 7, and it is taken to the department for police. In Article 4 it is put under Article 6. Does this mean that this is a definite separation from the Tiger unit from the competence of the minister and putting this special unit in the -- under the -- under the heading of the -- of all of police forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you, since these changes as well should be accompanied by a chart showing in which way the changes have occurred to look at 1D2323 of the Macedonian version, and 1D2409, which represents the chart of the -- work of the organisation of the interior ministry in the public safety, and we will pay special attention to those organs which are connected to the minister, is it correct that here on the top, we do not see the special unit Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. They are not there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at this -- this big rectangle, do you see now that in addition to the posebna unit, now we have an addition of the special tasks unit, Tiger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this way, the Tiger has stopped to be in direct connection and under the immediate competence of the minister as it was with the case with the previous book of rules?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if someone would say that in August while this is a chart from August 2001, when the changes were adopted to the book of rules and as it can be seen this happened in August 21, 2001. So if someone would say that at that time the Lions unit were in the structure of the police forces, this would not be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, therefore, both these book of rules and the accompanying chart clearly show that the Lions did not exist on this August 21st, 2001, but they were established, as you said, on October 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe before we break, I would like to tender this document, 1D213 an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As Exhibit 1D66, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have completed the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We must have the break now and resume at 20 minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, only two things. The document, the decision of the president from June 4th, 2001, which was in tab number 2, was accepted as exhibit 1D58. Since the high level of confidentiality of this document, I would like to tender it under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. It will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, secondly, for the sake of the transcript, in June -- June 15th, when the witness was displayed the document (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, I'm sorry, I did not get the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters. Therefore, on Friday, while the witness was displayed the (redacted) on page of the transcript 2.177, from 17th to 25 lines, and page -- page 2178, lines 1 to 6 and lines 12 to 16 the word "posebna" was used. This word should not appear in the transcript because the word "posebna" was not said and it is -- it cannot be found in the document which was displayed. We were speaking about the special unit Tigers. Since, after the witness -- the testifying of this witness we will have a clear situation and that we will not have any -- such mistakes in the transcript, I thought would be good to -- for the record to point out such a situation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we must wait until the record is corrected, from the Chamber's point of view. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we move into private session for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, dear witness M-056. My name is Antonio Apostolski and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, we represent Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Today I will ask you some questions which I think you can answer to and all with the purpose of giving a right image of the factual situation. To my learned colleague of the Prosecution, you said that with your unit you were deployed in Vaksince. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were before Vaksince and -- at the beginning of the Vaksince village from the Lojane village site.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The objective of your deployment was to arrest terrorist groups. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: These were members of the terrorist group the NLA. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you have participated to other actions for -- to neutralise and to destroy the terrorist groups of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the tactics of the terrorist groups of the NLA was after the completion of terrorist acts to retrieve in villages inhabited by civilian Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have personally seen the way they throw their uniforms at the -- as civilians they enter their houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: They were doing that in order to avoid arrest and to avoid criminal responsibility. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. And they knew that we would not use any forceful actions against civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was this the reason why Macedonian security forces appealed to the civilian population of Vaksince to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said you had participated to several actions against the NLA terrorist groups. Did -- during such actions you had close encounters with NLA terrorist members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you see what kind of light infantry weapons they used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had basically Kalashnikovs from automatic rifles but they had also some more sophisticated weapons made by -- from American and German origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the NLA members mostly used automatic rifles, type Kalashnikov, Chinese production?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. Such Kalashnikov -- penetrating flakjacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that it originated from Albanian Kosovo? I refer here to the Kalashnikovs produced in China.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that weapon mostly came from Albanian Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you aware that with such weapon -- this was the weapons used by the Albanian army from the communist region from the time of Enver Hodza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1996 there were troubles in Albania when the -- the military warehouses were robbed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know this very well. This was also in the media, and the media mentioned very large number of weapons that were stolen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you see how the NLA terrorist group members were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had different kind of uniforms. They had camouflage uniforms and black uniforms. The camouflage uniforms originated from the -- they were like the ex-Yugoslav uniforms, ex-army-- Yugoslav army uniforms. Some were of German origin and some were of an American origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct -- did the NLA members use a black -- a black clothes during the actions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours on page 36, line 1 of the transcript it reads "Albanian Kosovo," and the question should read "from Albania and Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: To -- to a question asked from my learned colleague the Prosecutor, you said that when each party would come to power the high officials would employ as body-guards members of party security. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, until now everyone has practiced this. After being employed in party security, they would be afterwards employed in the interior ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In that way on 2001 VMRO-DPMNE was in power and at that time the body-guards of high officials were members of party security teams of VMRO-DPMNE who previously were employed in PSOLO. This is a security unit. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In 2002, following the elections that took place on the 15th of September, the Social Democratic Alliance came to power with an abbreviation SDSM. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: They also did not keep the body-guards from the previous government for their own officials. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that as body-guards, people have taken people from the political party security from SDSM?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that they have been employed in the sector for security of individuals and premises within the MOI, the so-called PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that some of them have been directly hired as civilians and some of them came from other police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was this just a formal condition in order for them to enjoy their rights from employment, such as salary, health care and social insurance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. They were employed in order to provide security for their -- for their superiors, as it was the case earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: To my learned colleague from the Prosecution you told that the Macedonian population from the western part of Macedonia was displaced. Is it correct that the reason for this displacement was the pressure coming from the terrorist groups of NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there have been Macedonian civilians who have been kidnapped in this particular part of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there have been kidnapping and molestation of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that people have been also tortured and civilians who were raped, members of the Macedonian ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And also there are certain people who have been kidnapped and their destiny is not yet known.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that houses have been set on fire of Macedonian population that has been displaced by the terrorist NLA groups in order for these people not to come back in their own houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the tactic in order to burn down all the Macedonian houses in order for people not to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there are still displaced people from the ethnic Macedonian majority who still live in shelters and have not returned to their homes, because they're afraid about their security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's still internally displaced Macedonians who are not able to go back to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to Vaksince, is this the village in the vicinity of the city of Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall maybe that Kumanovo back in 2001 had certain problems with supply of water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The terrorists discontinued water supply because the water came from the lake of Lipkovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. In the beginning of my cross-examination, you told me that following the activities, the terrorist groups used to put on civilian clothes. Was it normal for men, civilians, to conduct paraffin tests in order to establish whether some of them fired a weapon or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is quite a normal regular police procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the people who had a positive paraffin test were being detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I'm informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that people with negative paraffin tests were released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you aware about any other method that was applied or used in the Republic of Macedonia in order to establish alleged use of fire-arms besides the paraffin test?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never worked in the forensics department. However, I believe there is no other method.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-056, a few minutes ago my colleague asked you about the practice of each time a new political party comes to power, such as in 2001 Macedonia, then that party would bring their so-called security staff which would be employed in the Ministry of the Interior. And I'd like to explore that with you for a moment, please. Was this practice done to ensure that those persons employed as body-guards in the Ministry of Interior would be loyal to the minister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Always body-guards have been brought there who, amongst other, they were always with the same people, each in opposition, because you cannot just leave the people who are working for the previous political party, and that is quite a normal procedure, as far as I'm informed, present in many other countries around the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What you mean by, "You cannot just leave the people who are working for the previous political party?" What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have this rule that the body-guard following the four years, cannot be as careful as he was earlier, because their jobs become routine and that is why they are being replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. So the body-guards from the party leaving power are replaced by persons affiliated with the party coming into power, who are believed will be more careful. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the entire security forces, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. You told my colleague a short time ago that we, the security forces, would not use any forceful actions against the civilian population. Suppose members of the security forces thought that certain civilians had something behind them. That was the term that you used with us last week. Then, in 2001, might security forces sometimes have used forces against such persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? Quite often we have been attacked from windows from houses, people, civilians used to live there, people without uniforms, and whenever we dealt with civilians we would check their personal identity, relations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that information, but you didn't answer my question. I'll repeat my question. Here it is again. What would happen in 2001 if members of the security forces thought that the so-called civilians "had something behind them"? Then might force have been used against these persons? You can just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if they are armed and if they resist arrest. Only then force can be used or so -- people if they are using fire-arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So if someone did not -- was not armed and was not resisting arrest, force, physical force, should not have been used against that person in 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is generally so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we move into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tab 16, which was Prosecution Exhibit P74, if you take a look at the Macedonian version -- actually, yeah, the Macedonian version. This is a document about the decision to establish a rapid intervention police battalion, the Ministry of Internal Affairs. The date up at the top is the 6th of August, 2001. And I'd like to look again with you at the preamble, please. Because the preamble says that based on Article 5, et cetera, et cetera, of the law on the organisation and work of state administration agencies, item 2 of the decision of the government of the Republic of Macedonia, to establish a unit for special purposes and part one, item 1.2 of the decision of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, to establish a temporary unit for combat against terrorism, et cetera, the minister of internal affairs brought the following decision. So would it be fair to say, Mr. M-056, that by issuing this decision, Minister Boskoski was effectively following his chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, it says here that the minister of interior of internal affairs was bringing this decision pursuant to several laws and a decision of the government of the Republic of Macedonia and a decision of the president of the Republic of Macedonia. So can we agree that Mr. Boskoski was doing his duty to follow the instructions of persons or institutions that governed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I need to ask you something. During her cross-examination, my colleague showed you a number of books of rules and amendments to rules of the Ministry of Interior. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Rules on the organisation of the ministry, et cetera, such as Exhibit 1D65. Why did the Ministry of Interior have so many rules?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For every single issue we have our rule books, for all the changes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. During the crisis time in 2000 -- of 2001, were the rules in the Ministry of Interior always followed to the letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I am informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you turn please to tab 20 in that binder. This document became Exhibit 1D62. It's dated the 5th of September, 2001. And it deals with amendments to the rules on the organisation of the work of the Ministry of the Interior. Do you recall telling my colleague, Ms. Residovic, that it would have been impossible -- let me step back for a minute. That the procedures outlined in these rules had to be completed before the Lions unit could operate. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So would it have been impossible for these Lions units to have existed or operated before these official changes to the rules in September of 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-056 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and not before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us please --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I don't want to do the wrong thing. Can you tell me whether we are in public or private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Public.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I was saying that that now concludes the questions that are to be asked of you. As a consequence, you are now, of course, free to return to your home and your ordinary occupations. You will be shown out by the court officer, and we would thank you for your attendance in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's a question whether it would be profitable to deal with any issues that are of concern at this point or whether we move straight to the next witness. Is there any pressing matter that any counsel wishes to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one matter. Is it not a pressing one. It relates to the three Prosecution application for withdrawal of witnesses. What we would be ready to do with the leave of the Chamber would be to answer perhaps after this witness if my colleague wants to starts with Dr. Jakovski. We could do that at any time tomorrow or Wednesday at your convenience. And we will try to do all three applications at once, if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, because that is the matter which the Chamber thought was most pressing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And we have to formally seek an extension of time, Your Honour, because of the fact that we are late in relation to the first application. We've been moved forward by the course of the evidence and we'll formally seek leave tomorrow when we address the Court on those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the chamber also mention that regrettably we find we are now unable to sit past 6.00 on Wednesday. Another matter affecting other Judges compels us to be available at that time. We would expect therefore we will have two sessions from 2.15 on Wednesday, stretching each one to the patience and limits, the capacity of the technical people. We should be able to sit for an hour and 35 minutes or a little bit more in each session, but that will bring us to approximately 6.00. We will then adjourn. By that means we will considerably limit the time that we would lose to only half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps while I'm on my feet, I would just indicate to Your Honours that there is a number of procedural matter which we would like to address prior to Mr. Hutsch starting his evidence on Wednesday or Thursday, whenever that will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If that should arise, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation which is on the card given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Jakovski. Sir, is your name Dr. Zlatko Jakovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Zlatko Jakovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you tell us, please, briefly what is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: In 1997, I graduated from the faculty of medicine, and the title I earned was doctor of medical sciences. In 2001, I have completed by specialisation in forensic medicine, and the title I earned was a specialist in forensic medicine. Since 1999 I'm a junior assistant at the medical faculty in Skopje. Since 2002, I earned the title of an M.Sc. in medical sciences in the area of forensic ballistics. From 2003, I'm a senior assistant at the faculty of medicine in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you a medical doctor by profession?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I am a medical doctor by profession.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And as a medical doctor, do you also have a specialisation in forensic medicine?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm a specialist in forensic medicine since 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And with that specialisation, do you perform autopsies at the faculty of medicine in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I perform autopsies at the faculty of medicine in Skopje, about 70 to 90 autopsies per year. The total of autopsies I have performed or participated in is about thousand.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the total number of autopsies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And have all those been performed at the faculty of medicine in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Some of them at the faculty of medicine in Skopje while some were in the medical centres across Macedonia because our institute covers also larger part of the territory of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And as part of conducting an autopsy, do you also -- as doctor in forensic medicine, do you also -- or are you called upon to determine the cause of death?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
