utterances.text: Yes. One of the tasks of the autopsy is to establish the cause of death.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And as part of the autopsy and establishing the cause of death, are you also called upon to determine the nature and type of injuries that may be found on a particular body that you autopsy?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And when you perform an autopsy specifically with respect to your position at the faculty of medicine in Skopje, where does the request for an autopsy come from?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: According -- pursuant to the criminal court of the Republic of Macedonia, an autopsy can be requested by an investigating judge or pursuant to the law on health care of the Republic of Macedonia, the medical institution where the patient has died.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: When you conduct an autopsy, do you also prepare a written report with respect to your findings?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. On any autopsy, there is a section protocol or autopsy report performed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to this witness because of the nature of exhibits that I will seek to tender, we have prepared binders for the Court. If we could distribute those now, please, with the assistance the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we please --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if could you refer to tab 1 of the binder that's in front of you. It is 65 ter 13.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this particular report has already been admitted as P00049. I refer to the 65 ter number for purposes of e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Doctor, could you please look at the documents that are displayed in front of you. Do you recognise the protocol -- let me just start at the top here in the left corner. It says "Institute for Forensic Medicine and Criminology at the medical faculty, Skopje," and it's also dated 14 August 2001 in the upper left-hand corner. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in the middle it is in bold, it says "section protocol." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then at the beginning of a that paragraph it says: "About a forensic expertise carried out on the corpse of the deceased," and it says "Atulla Qaili, at the age of around 35 to 40 years with residence at village Ljuboten." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we can turn to the last page of this document, which is page 9 in the English, page 12 of the Macedonian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, witness, you can also refer to the hard copies that are in front of you if it is easier. If I could direct your attention to the bottom of this page, there is a couple of signatures. It says Professor Dr. Aleksa Duma and then below that it says teaching assistant Dr. Zlatko Jakovski. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recognise this particular protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this is a protocol for an autopsy that you yourself conducted?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, together with the Professor Aleksa Duma on the body of the deceased Atulla Qaili.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And before we discuss this protocol, let me ask you first, do you recall who requested this particular autopsy of Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: This was on the request of the general city hospital of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Answer when you receive a request, for instance in this case from the city hospital of Skopje, would you get paperwork with respect to that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: From the city General Hospital in Skopje, we received the mortuary note where the request for autopsy was written.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention, witness, to tab 2 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could please display on e-court what is already P 0046. It is actually 65 ter 10.54, and this particular document is located at the Macedonian translation in e-court. I'm sorry. Is there a -- there should be a document that only displays the upper half of this page. That is located at the Macedonian translation for 65 ter 10.54. Could we display that, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, doctor, do you see the Macedonian document that is before you, and in the --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At the top it says, "To the pathology anatomy institute, Skopje," and in the middle there it says "autopsy needed" and then in bold it says "death certificate" and indicates clinic surgery general city hospital, Skopje. And it says name and last name, Abdula Cajani do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Does this piece of paper look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the request related to the autopsy of the person Qaili Atulla.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at some point in time, did you realise or did you come to know that this Abdula Cajani is the same person that you've referred to the autopsy protocol that we see as Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: We realised it was the same person after several days when the family of the deceased requested a document so that they are able to bury him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in most cases, is this typically the only paperwork, what is before you now, is that the only paperwork that you would receive with the deceased at the time the request for autopsy is made?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: In most of the cases we only receive the mortuary note, but sometimes we are also submitted the discharge note from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what information is typically reflected in what you have termed the discharge note from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: The discharge note from the hospital or the mortuary note indicates the personal data of the patient, also the diagnosis at admission, any medical interventions performed, in the sense of laboratory tests, X-ray, any surgeries performed, if the cause of death has been identified, and the time of death.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And with respect to the autopsy request for Atulla Qaili, though, was this piece of paper that is displayed before you that the only piece of paper that accompanied the body at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: When you performed the autopsy on Atulla Qaili, did you take notes of your findings?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Notes are taken regarding the autopsy. There are special charts for that, where any changes that are observed in the course of the autopsy are recorded. And on -- at the other side of that page, of those charts, notes are taken about the internal findings.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. Are these notes then incorporated into what you've termed the final autopsy protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Any change observed and recorded in the charts is described in detail in the section protocol, in Macedonian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If you could please turn to tab 3 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could display, please, 65 ter 993?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Dr. Jakovski, do you see the sketch or the paperwork that is in front of you. It has some handwritten notes on it, and it has basically a sketch of the front and back of the human body. There's also some handwritten numbers or dimensions. Do you recognise the handwriting on this particular document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do. These are sketches made by me in the course of the autopsy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is this in the course of a specific autopsy, that is, with respect to Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, what do these markings indicate? I see that have you circles or, loosely term them circles, on -- marked on the front and back side of the body that is depicted here. What do those markings indicate?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: In this way, you record the injuries found on the body, their appearance and location.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: The measurements, as well as the abbreviations for contusion or excoriation or haematoma. For instance, X would mean excoriation, H would mean a haematoma, CONT would mean contusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you please -- maybe perhaps we could just simply define these terms one by one. You noted excoriation, which would be EX on this diagram. Could you tell in just layperson's terms what that would mean?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: It's excoriation. Excoriation would then mean --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the doctor is just translating the words in Macedonian from the medical Latin. Haematoma is a haematoma. I can't translate it differently?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Excoriation is a layer of skin being ripped.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's comment, it is again a translation of these terms in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: With respect to a haematoma, would that be loosely termed as a bruise?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And with respect to a contusion, is that -- what is difference between that and basically a haematoma, if could you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: The haematoma is blood spilling outside of the blood vessels into the subcutaneous fat tissue. And a contusion is a sheet of skin being ripped off, accompanied by a haematoma.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI
utterances.text: So, in the case of a contusion we have both haematoma and excoriation, or otherwise known as a sheet of skin missing, and that is what a contusion means.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. Perhaps this might be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Ms. Motoike. We must adjourn now for the day and resume tomorrow at 2.15. Doctor, I'm sorry, but we've come to the end of our sitting day, and we would ask you if could you continue tomorrow at 2.15. Thank you. We now adjourn for the evening.
